author: Y Combinator
description:
Applied Electrodynamics is building cameras that can see through walls and other opaque materials.

Using radio waves, their system can see through drywall, marble, and other surfaces to locate studs, pipes, cables, junction boxes, and other objects hidden behind them, then turn that data into a dimensionally accurate 3D model.
title: A camera that can see through walls

author: Y Combinator
description:
This week's Paper Club is all about alternative compute. We cover the case for abandoning backprop and the gradient-free optimizer being built to replace it, how the propagation of light can be programmed to run a diffusion model, where neuromorphic computing really stands in 2026, and how human brain cells on a chip learned to play Doom.

Sign up for the next Paper Club, where we'll discuss AI Safety: https://events.ycombinator.com/yc-paperclub-oct7
